# Historical evidence synthesis: scene_rsi_v3__H06, batch 1 of 1

## Scope and coverage

This batch covers all **three inventoried source files**, each a student trajectory with 30 units. S0354 and S0355 were audited in two chunks each; S0356 was audited in one. The supplied reports, not the raw trajectories or images, are the basis for this synthesis. Chunk-local visibility limits can be resolved where another supplied chunk reports the later events, but they do not supply the missing reference images or renders. File counts are not counts of independent trials: copies, if present, would not establish independence.

Original paths below share this prefix:
`/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H06/selection/`

## Evidence matrix

| Source and original path suffix | Executed attempt and validation | Outcome and limits |
|---|---|---|
| **S0354**, `bw_0045/1/trajectory.jsonl` | Three successive scene builds. After two renders, the student changed camera and scene geometry; the third build and render succeeded and step 3 was selected (lines 3–4, 9, 13–14, 19, 23–30). Its final landmark comparison improved muzzle and rump errors but worsened door and wall-junction errors (line 29). | Technical success and mixed numerical results; visual fidelity and formal task success unknown. The first chunk alone ended at build start, but the second reports completion, so this is not an established interruption. |
| **S0355**, `bw_0017/1/trajectory.jsonl` | Three builds and renders; camera, shell and object revisions followed the student’s render diagnoses. Step 3 succeeded and was selected (lines 3–10, 11–20, 21–30). Its reported tank-top projection improved, while all four final camera comparisons were labeled worse than baseline (line 29). | Technical success with a local numerical improvement and camera regressions; overall reconstruction quality and formal success unknown. |
| **S0356**, `bw_0031/1/trajectory.jsonl` | Three builds, renders and selections. The student revised camera, room and desk parameters, then camera, lighting and finishes (lines 3–10, 11–20, 21–30). The final output reported three landmarks closer and three farther than baseline (line 29). | Technical success with mixed projection results; visual fidelity and formal success unknown. No subsequent visual review is visible. |

## Comparison of attempts and outcomes

All three students produced **nonempty executed scene programs**, followed by revisions and technically successful renders. Selection of the final step records acceptance within the workflow, not an independent correctness judgment. None of the supplied audits establishes a failed build, empty patch, permission or branch stop, CLI stop, timeout, or interrupted final execution. Nor does a worsening landmark establish an algorithmic failure or an overall failed reconstruction. These absent categories should not be inferred merely to complete a comparison: the observed contrast is between technical completion and partial, mixed numerical alignment, with visual task outcomes unknown.

In S0354, the student interpreted the reference as a dairy barn and built cows, dividers, architecture and a worker. After render feedback, it revised the camera and geometry; its second comparison improved some points while worsening divider-bend and wall-junction errors (lines 3–4, 11–19). The third result reports muzzle error falling from 0.418 to 0.174 and rump error from 0.469 to 0.109, while door error rose from 0.271 to 0.310 and wall-junction error from 0.240 to 0.255 (line 29). These are reported comparisons against estimated correspondences, not verified silhouettes or overall image quality.

In S0355, the student interpreted an indoor image as an industrial hall, with machinery, tank, conveyors and architecture. Its second camera comparison improved the machine-top projection while worsening window, tank and conveyor points (lines 3–4, 11–20). At step 3, the tank-top projection moved nearer the stated reference, but the log labeled all four final camera comparisons worse than baseline (line 29). The local tank result therefore cannot be generalized into overall improvement.

In S0356, the student interpreted the image as a control-room photograph with a separate GRID panel, whose placement was speculative. On revised geometry, the second camera check reported four points closer and one farther; the final check reported three closer and three farther (lines 3, 19, 29). These comparisons are not clean comparisons of the complete old and new scenes. The student's reported wall occlusion and washed-out appearance motivated further changes, but the supplied audit cannot independently confirm those visual diagnoses or their repair.

## Guidance, adoption and quality

No separate teacher message, diagnosis, proposed patch, receipt or teacher execution is visible in any of the three trajectories. That is an observation about this batch, not proof that teacher advice could never have existed outside the recorded material. The task and runner did deliver procedural or render-comparison instructions. S0354 visibly used inventory comments and projection tables; S0355 revised after receiving the reference, render and execution output; S0356's inventories, projection checks and revisions show partial adoption of delivered instructions (respectively S0354 lines 1–4, 11–14, 21–24; S0355 lines 11–14, 21–24; S0356 lines 1, 11, 21–24).

In each case, the student's diagnosis is distinct from both the executed update and its validation. Code and logs establish that updates were run and renders selected; they do not independently establish that the identified defects were real or that the updates fixed them. Named parts and object hierarchies likewise do not prove visible connections, correct pose or semantic identity. The images are unavailable to this audit, so material appearance, texture, lighting, occlusion, framing and overall resemblance remain unverified. Missing formal scores are **unknown**, not failures or successes; old model cost cannot be recovered from its absence.

## Transferable constraints and boundaries

- **Execution, selection and visual correctness are separate evidence levels.** All three final renders completed and were selected, but none has independently observed image quality or a formal success score in the supplied reports.
- **Multiple point checks can reveal competing changes.** All three trajectories report landmark trade-offs. That supports treating such checks as limited numerical evidence, not as substitutes for image comparison or proof of better overall framing.
- **The particular objects and proposed causes are task-specific.** Cow and door landmarks, a tank adjustment, and a control-room wall are not general facts about other scenes. Camera placement, lighting and geometry as causes of the students' reported defects remain hypotheses here.
- **Do not overgeneralize adoption or failure.** Students used delivered runner feedback, but no separate teacher intervention is evidenced. Mixed projections are counterexamples to equating a successful render—or one improved anchor—with a uniformly improved scene; they are not proof that the final scenes failed.

This is an audit-only synthesis and does not enter capability generation.
